variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An AI safety and guardrails system is the policy, enforcement, evidence, and response layer around an AI model. It decides what the application may read, produce, or change; checks the result against declared risk boundaries; and records enough evidence for review and incident response.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Start with a risk contract”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Policy boundary
pairs.detail: Define allowed behavior, forbidden behavior, exceptions, risk tiers, and the owner who can change the contract.
pairs.explanation: Define allowed behavior, forbidden behavior, exceptions, risk tiers, and the owner who can change the contract.

pairs.label: Enforcement boundary
pairs.detail: Apply authorization, least privilege, structured validation, rate limits, approvals, and deterministic tool mediation.
pairs.explanation: Apply authorization, least privilege, structured validation, rate limits, approvals, and deterministic tool mediation.

pairs.label: Evidence boundary
pairs.detail: Version evaluation cases, decisions, overrides, incidents, policy changes, and the exact system configuration.
pairs.explanation: Version evaluation cases, decisions, overrides, incidents, policy changes, and the exact system configuration.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is a missing or uncertain control must never silently grant high-impact authority.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Policy boundary: Define allowed behavior, forbidden behavior, exceptions, risk tiers, and the owner who can change the contract. Enforcement boundary: Apply authorization, least privilege, structured validation, rate limits, approvals, and deterministic tool mediation. Evidence boundary: Version evaluation cases, decisions, overrides, incidents, policy changes, and the exact system configuration.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Operate guardrails as a versioned control plane”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Observe
pairs.detail: Monitor policy outcomes, slice metrics, tool denials, overrides, user reports, drift, and queue health.
pairs.explanation: Monitor policy outcomes, slice metrics, tool denials, overrides, user reports, drift, and queue health.

pairs.label: Contain
pairs.detail: Disable a capability, lower exposure, switch to answer-only mode, or roll back the model and policy bundle.
pairs.explanation: Disable a capability, lower exposure, switch to answer-only mode, or roll back the model and policy bundle.

pairs.label: Investigate
pairs.detail: Replay the versioned path, identify the failed boundary, estimate affected users, and preserve access-controlled evidence.
pairs.explanation: Replay the versioned path, identify the failed boundary, estimate affected users, and preserve access-controlled evidence.

pairs.label: Improve
pairs.detail: Add regression cases, repair the control, review related paths, rehearse the response, and earn exposure again.
pairs.explanation: Add regression cases, repair the control, review related paths, rehearse the response, and earn exposure again.

variants.prompt: Why is an output classifier alone not a guardrails system?
options: Output classifiers cannot return confidence scores
It cannot independently constrain data access, tool authority, approvals, and incident response
Classifiers only work on images
A model cannot call application tools
variants.explanation: Guardrails are a system of independent boundaries. Content evaluation cannot replace authorization, least privilege, complete mediation, or operational response.
optionFeedback: Guardrails are a system of independent boundaries. Content evaluation cannot replace authorization, least privilege, complete mediation, or operational response.
